question: A 55-year-old patient describes a pulsatile whooshing sound in his right ear that is synchronous with his heartbeat. On examination, the sound disappears on compression of the ipsilateral jugular vein. Which type of tinnitus does this represent and what is the most important cause to exclude?

answers.text: Subjective tinnitus due to inner ear hair cell damage from ageing

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Subjective tinnitus is heard only by the patient and has no audible correlate. This patient's tinnitus is pulsatile, synchronous with the heartbeat, and audibly altered by jugular vein compression — defining features of objective pulsatile tinnitus with a vascular aetiology, not presbycusis.

answers.text: Objective pulsatile tinnitus; a vascular lesion such as a glomus jugulare tumour must be excluded

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Objective pulsatile tinnitus that synchronises with the heartbeat and changes with jugular compression indicates a vascular source. A glomus jugulare (paraganglioma) is a critical diagnosis to exclude, as it is a vascular tumour of the jugular bulb. CT/MRI with angiography is mandatory. Other causes include arteriovenous malformations, carotid stenosis, and high jugular bulb.

answers.text: Tinnitus due to Eustachian tube dysfunction with middle ear effusion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Eustachian tube dysfunction causes a low-pitched, often intermittent, non-pulsatile tinnitus associated with conductive hearing loss and a type B tympanogram. It is not synchronous with the heartbeat and is not affected by jugular vein compression.

Incorrect. Pulsatile tinnitus synchronous with the heartbeat is never psychogenic. It has a specific vascular or anatomical cause that must be investigated urgently. Labelling it psychogenic before completing a vascular workup is a serious clinical error.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: pulsatile tinnitus = vascular cause until proven otherwise. Glomus jugulare is the key diagnosis to exclude. The jugular compression test (disappears on compression) confirms venous origin. Imaging workup (CT temporal bone + MRI/MRA) is mandatory.

Correct. Pulsatile tinnitus synchronous with the heartbeat is objective and vascular. Glomus jugulare, AVM, carotid stenosis, and high jugular bulb must be excluded with imaging. Never dismiss pulsatile tinnitus as psychogenic.
